_comment: One job per STRIP — the whole strip as one image, for the concept run. Run with comic_render.py --provider runway|google|openai.

jobs.title: The job
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 20, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer. WOOD usually wears brown canvas chore coat with a frayed cuff and one mismatched button, hands in its pockets, plain tee, dark jeans. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: A HELP WANTED sign on 101. Wood applies with a monologue. He gets it anyway. Panel 1: a low roadside building with a sign reading HECETA FRAME & MATTING on a coastal highway, a HELP WANTED card in the window, an old Datsun pulling in, brush-pen black and white (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: the interior of a small picture-framing shop with frames covering the walls, a woman in reading glasses at a mat cutter, a young man in a chore coat talking in the doorway (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "I should say up front that I consider the frame a form of criticism. What you exclude is—". Owner says "Can you cut a forty-five.". Panel 3: close-up of a young man's hands guiding a mat cutter through a clean forty-five-degree corner on mat board (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: a woman in reading glasses holding a cut mat corner up to the light and speaking flatly to a young man. Owner says "Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays. Eight-fifty. Don't talk to the customers about criticism.". Wood says "What about—". Owner says "Or film.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17.
